component.name: cxfrs
component.title: CXF-RS
component.description: Expose REST services described by JAX-RS resource classes, or send requests to REST services, using Apache CXF.
component.label: rest

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

synchronous.label: producer,advanced
synchronous.description: Whether to always process the exchange synchronously. If true, the producer sends each request without an InvocationCallback and waits for the response, and the consumer runs the route without a CXF continuation. The component sets the value on each endpoint that it creates, including a bean: endpoint, unless the endpoint URI sets synchronous.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

headerFilterStrategy.label: filter
headerFilterStrategy.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.spi.HeaderFilterStrategy to filter header to and from Camel message.

useGlobalSslContextParameters.label: security
useGlobalSslContextParameters.description: Whether to use the global SSL context parameters of the CamelContext for each endpoint that the component creates and that has no sslContextParameters. The producer uses them for the HTTPS requests that it sends. The consumer does not use them.

CamelDestinationOverrideUrl.description: The address that the producer sends the request to, in place of the service address. With the cxf component, the HTTP transport of CXF uses it, and the Camel transport does not.

CamelAuthentication.description: The authenticated user of the request, as a Subject. The consumer sets it from the SecurityContext of the CXF request message: the Subject of a LoginSecurityContext, or else a new Subject with the user Principal.

CamelHttpMethod.description: The HTTP method of the request, for example GET. The consumer sets it to the method of the request. With the WebClient API, the producer sends its request with this method, and without an entity for GET.

CamelHttpPath.description: The path of the request below the service address, for example /customers/123. The consumer sets it to the path of the request below the service address. With the WebClient API, the producer appends it to the service address or to the address in the CamelDestinationOverrideUrl header, and fills template variables such as {id} in this path with the values of the CamelCxfRsVarValues header.

Content-Type.description: The Content-Type of the message body. The consumer sets it to the Content-Type of the request, and uses it as the Content-Type of the response when the message body of the reply is not a jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response. The consumer does not use this header for the response when synchronous is true or when it gets no continuation from the transport. The producer sends it as the Content-Type of its request. When synchronous is false, or when the producer reads the response as a Response, it copies the response headers to the reply, and a Content-Type of the response replaces this header.

CamelHttpQuery.description: The query string of the request, without the question mark, for example id=1&name=a%20b. The consumer sets it when the request has a query string. With the WebClient API, the producer sends the parameters of this query string in place of the query parameters of the endpoint URI that are not options, unless the CamelCxfRsQueryMap header is set.

CamelHttpResponseCode.description: The HTTP status code of the response. The producer sets it to the status code of the response, unless the exchange pattern is InOnly or the exchange fails, which with the default settings happens for a status code greater than 207. On the consumer, the route sets it to choose the status code of the response when the message body of the reply is not a jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response. If not set, the status code of the response is 200 for a successful reply, or 204 for a reply without a message body when bindingStyle is Default.

Content-Encoding.description: The Content-Encoding of the message body, for example gzip. The consumer sets it to the Content-Encoding of the request, unless CXF has already decompressed the request, for example with a GZIPFeature. The producer sends it as the Content-Encoding of its request. When synchronous is false, or when the producer reads the response as a jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response, it copies the response headers to the reply, and a Content-Encoding of the response replaces this header, unless CXF has already decompressed the response. The consumer and the producer do not compress or decompress the message body because of this header.

org.apache.cxf.message.Message.PROTOCOL_.description: The HTTP headers to add to the response of the consumer, as a Map from the header name to a List of values or to one value. The consumer adds them when the message body of the reply is not a jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response, and the Content-Type header replaces the Content-Type entry of the Map. The consumer ignores the entries of the Map when synchronous is true or when it gets no continuation from the transport. The consumer does not put the HTTP headers of the request into this Map: each HTTP header of the request that the header filter strategy keeps becomes a separate Camel header.

CamelCxfMessage.description: The CXF request message, as an org.apache.cxf.message.Message. The consumer sets it for each request. With the WebClient API, the producer adds the matrix parameters in the request URI of this message to the end of the path of its own request.

CamelCxfRsUsingHttpAPI.description: Whether to use the CXF WebClient API instead of the proxy-based API for this message. This header replaces the httpClientAPI option.

CamelCxfRsVarValues.description: The values of the template variables in the path of the request, as an Object[], in the order in which the variables appear. With the WebClient API, the producer fills the variables such as {id} in the CamelHttpPath header with them. With the proxy-based API, the producer passes them to CXF for the variables in the Path annotation of the first resource class, and a PathParam or BeanParam parameter of the resource method can take precedence for one of these variables.

CamelCxfRsResponseClass.description: The class to read the response entity as, for example String. The consumer sets it to the return type of the resource method. The producer uses it only with the WebClient API, where the message body of the reply is the jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response if this header is not set or is Response.

CamelCxfRsResponseGenericType.description: The generic type to read the response entity as, given as a java.lang.reflect.Type. The consumer sets it to the generic return type of the resource method. The producer uses it only with the WebClient API, and only when the CamelCxfRsResponseClass header is a class other than jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response. When synchronous is true, the producer uses it only for a Collection response class, and this header must then be a ParameterizedType whose first type argument is the class of the elements.

CamelCxfRsQueryMap.description: The query parameters of the request, as a Map from the parameter name to the value. With the WebClient API, the producer sends them in place of the CamelHttpQuery header and of the query parameters of the endpoint URI that are not options, even when the Map is empty.

CamelCxfRsOperationResourceInfoStack.description: The resource methods and sub-resource locators that CXF matched for the request, as a copy of the org.apache.cxf.jaxrs.model.OperationResourceInfoStack, which holds one MethodInvocationInfo for each of them, with the root resource at the bottom of the stack. The consumer sets it for each request. The producer does not use it.

consumerOut.description: Default: a MessageContentsList of the parameters of the resource method, with its name in the CamelCxfOperationName header. SimpleConsumer: the request entity as the method declares it (a String, an InputStream, a JAXB bean), with the path, query and header parameters in headers; the MessageContentsList when the method has no entity, such as a GET

consumerReply.description: The response entity: a jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response, or text, bytes, a stream, a file, or an object a JAX-RS provider writes for the Content-Type (a JAXB bean as XML); a Map or a List fails without a provider for it. With the Default binding an unchanged request MessageContentsList replies with its single element, or no content when empty (unless the method returns a collection); one of several parameters fails: set the reply body

producerIn.description: The request entity, written for the Content-Type header: text, bytes, a stream, a file or an object a JAX-RS provider writes, such as a List as a whole (of a MessageContentsList or an Object[] only the first element is sent); a Map fails. A GET sends no body. With httpClientAPI=false: the parameters of the resource method named by the CamelCxfOperationName header, as a List or the one parameter

producerOut.description: A jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response whose entity is the response stream, read once (it converts to a String or an InputStream); the entity read as the class in the CamelCxfRsResponseClass header when that is set. With httpClientAPI=false: the return value of the resource method, null for a void one

beanId.description: The id of the registry bean that defines this endpoint. Written in the path of the endpoint URI in place of the service address, with the prefix bean:, for example bean:rsEndpoint. The bean is a CxfRsEndpoint, or, with camel-cxf-spring-rest, a CXF JAXRSServerFactoryBean for the consumer or a JAXRSClientFactoryBean for the producer, for example from a cxf:rsServer or cxf:rsClient element in Spring XML. The options of the endpoint URI are applied after the settings of the bean. On a CxfRsEndpoint bean, they are applied to the bean itself, so endpoint URIs with different options must not share one CxfRsEndpoint bean.

address.description: The service address, for example http://localhost:9000/rest. The consumer receives requests at this address, and the producer sends requests to it. The CamelDestinationOverrideUrl header replaces this address for a request that the producer sends.

features.description: The CXF features to add to the server that the consumer creates and to each client that the producer creates, as a List of org.apache.cxf.feature.Feature. Written in the endpoint URI as bean ids with the prefix #, separated by commas, for example #gzipFeature, or as the id of one List bean, for example #myFeatures.

modelRef.description: The location of a CXF user model, for example classpath:/model/customers.xml. The model is an XML document that describes resources and their operations in place of JAX-RS annotations, and the name attribute of each resource names its resource class. On the consumer, one resource of the model can be without a name attribute: the consumer gives it the interface org.apache.camel.component.cxf.jaxrs.DefaultModelResource, which works only when performInvocation is false. The producer builds requests from the model only with the proxy-based API.

providers.description: The JAX-RS providers to add to the server that the consumer creates and to each client that the producer creates, for example a MessageBodyReader and MessageBodyWriter for JSON. Written in the endpoint URI as bean ids with the prefix #, separated by commas, for example #jsonProvider,#xmlProvider. The built-in CXF providers stay registered.

resourceClasses.description: The JAX-RS resource classes. Written in the endpoint URI as fully qualified class names, separated by commas. The consumer serves them as root resources, and a resource class can be an interface only when performInvocation is false. Without resource classes, the consumer needs other resources, for example from serviceBeans or modelRef. With the proxy-based API, the producer calls the resource method named by the CamelCxfOperationName header on a proxy of the first resource class. With the WebClient API, the producer does not need resource classes.

schemaLocations.description: Sets the locations of the schema(s) which can be used to validate the incoming XML or JAXB-driven JSON.

skipFaultLogging.description: Whether to skip the log entry that the PhaseInterceptorChain writes when an interceptor throws an exception. Sets the CXF property org.apache.cxf.logging.FaultListener to a FaultListener that skips this log entry. Other log entries that CXF writes while it handles the fault are not affected.

bindingStyle.label: consumer
bindingStyle.description: How the consumer maps the request to the Camel message and the reply to the response. Default: the message body is a MessageContentsList of the parameters of the resource method. SimpleConsumer: the path, query, header, cookie, form and matrix parameters become Camel headers named as in their annotations, and the first other parameter, normally the request entity, becomes the message body. The component documentation describes SimpleConsumer in detail. Custom: the CxfRsBinding of the binding option maps the request and the reply. Setting the binding option sets bindingStyle to Custom. The producer uses the binding that Default or Custom selects, and cannot be created with SimpleConsumer.

publishedEndpointUrl.label: consumer
publishedEndpointUrl.description: The address to publish in the WADL that the consumer serves at the service address followed by ?_wadl. It replaces the base attribute of the resources element. Use it when clients reach the service through another address, for example when the service is behind a proxy. CXF serves the WADL only when the module cxf-rt-rs-service-description is on the classpath.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer,advanced
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

serviceBeans.label: consumer,advanced
serviceBeans.description: The beans to serve as JAX-RS root resources of the consumer, in addition to resourceClasses. Written in the endpoint URI as bean ids with the prefix #, separated by commas, for example #customerService, or as the id of one List bean, for example #myServiceBeans. The consumer calls the resource methods of the beans only when performInvocation is true, but always calls their sub-resource locators.

cookieHandler.label: producer
cookieHandler.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.http.base.cookie.CookieHandler to keep the cookies of an HTTP session between the requests that the producer sends. An InstanceCookieHandler keeps the cookies in the handler itself, and an ExchangeCookieHandler keeps them in an exchange property. The consumer does not use it.

hostnameVerifier.label: producer
hostnameVerifier.description: To use a custom javax.net.ssl.HostnameVerifier for the HTTPS requests that the producer sends. The consumer does not use it.

sslContextParameters.label: producer
sslContextParameters.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.support.jsse.SSLContextParameters for the HTTPS requests that the producer sends. If not set, the component sets it to the global SSL context parameters when it creates the endpoint and its own useGlobalSslContextParameters option is true. The consumer does not use it.

throwExceptionOnFailure.label: producer
throwExceptionOnFailure.description: Whether to fail the exchange with an org.apache.camel.component.cxf.common.CxfOperationException when the HTTP status code of the response is greater than 207. The exception holds the status code, the response headers and the response entity. When synchronous is true, the producer does this only when it reads the response as a jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response. CXF itself can also fail the exchange for a status code of 300 or more, for example with the proxy-based API when the resource method does not return a Response.

httpClientAPI.label: producer,advanced
httpClientAPI.description: Whether to use the CXF WebClient API instead of the proxy-based API. With the WebClient API, the producer builds the request from the CamelHttpMethod and CamelHttpPath headers and, for methods such as POST and PUT, takes the request entity from the message body. With the proxy-based API, the producer calls the resource method named by the CamelCxfOperationName header on a proxy of the first resource class, with the message body as its parameters. The CamelCxfRsUsingHttpAPI header replaces this option for a request that the producer sends.

ignoreDeleteMethodMessageBody.label: producer,advanced
ignoreDeleteMethodMessageBody.description: Whether to ignore the message body for a DELETE request and send the request without an entity. If false, the producer takes the request entity of a DELETE request from the message body, as for POST and PUT. The producer uses this option only with the WebClient API.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

maxClientCacheSize.label: producer,advanced
maxClientCacheSize.description: The maximum number of CXF JAXRSClientFactoryBean instances that the producer keeps in its cache, one for each address that it sends requests to: the service address, or the address in the CamelDestinationOverrideUrl header. When the cache is full, the producer drops the least recently used factory bean. The producer creates a new client from the factory bean for each request. The value must be greater than 0.

synchronous.label: producer,advanced
synchronous.description: Whether to always process the exchange synchronously. If true, the producer sends each request without an InvocationCallback and waits for the response, and the consumer runs the route without a CXF continuation. The component sets it to the value of its own synchronous option when it creates the endpoint, including a bean: endpoint, unless the endpoint URI sets it.

binding.label: advanced
binding.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.component.cxf.jaxrs.CxfRsBinding to map between the Camel message and the JAX-RS request and response, on the consumer and on the producer. Setting this option sets bindingStyle to Custom.

bus.label: advanced
bus.description: To use a custom configured CXF Bus.

continuationTimeout.label: advanced
continuationTimeout.description: The timeout in milliseconds of the CXF continuation that the consumer uses to process the exchange asynchronously. If it expires before the route has completed, the consumer sets an ExchangeTimedOutException on the exchange and fails the request with this exception, which a JAX-RS ExceptionMapper can turn into a response. Use 0 for no timeout. Not used when synchronous is true or when the consumer gets no continuation from the transport.

cxfRsConfigurer.label: advanced
cxfRsConfigurer.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.component.cxf.jaxrs.CxfRsConfigurer to configure CXF in Java code. Its configure method receives the CXF factory bean before a client or the server is created, and configureClient receives each client that the producer creates. The consumer does not call configureServer.

defaultBus.label: advanced
defaultBus.description: Whether to set the Bus of the bus option as the CXF default bus by calling BusFactory.setDefaultBus. The endpoint makes this call when the bus option is set, so this option must be set before the bus option, which is the order in which an endpoint URI sets them. Without the bus option, this option has no effect, because the endpoint does not create a Bus.

headerFilterStrategy.label: advanced
headerFilterStrategy.description: To use a custom HeaderFilterStrategy to filter header to and from Camel message.

performInvocation.label: advanced
performInvocation.description: Whether to call the resource method, on an instance of the resource class or on a bean of serviceBeans, before the consumer runs the route. If true, the consumer does not serve resource classes that are interfaces. If the method throws an exception, the route does not run. If the method returns a value other than null, the route gets that value as the message body, without the Camel headers that the binding sets from the request.

propagateContexts.label: advanced
propagateContexts.description: Whether to set the JAX-RS contexts of the request as exchange properties, so that the route can use the JAX-RS API on them. The consumer sets the UriInfo, Request, HttpHeaders and SecurityContext of the request, each under the fully qualified name of its interface, for example jakarta.ws.rs.core.UriInfo.

loggingFeatureEnabled.label: logging
loggingFeatureEnabled.description: Whether to add a LoggingFeature, which writes the requests and responses of the endpoint to the log. The LoggingFeature writes them with SLF4J at INFO level to loggers whose names start with org.apache.cxf.services.

loggingSizeLimit.label: logging
loggingSizeLimit.description: The size limit at which CXF truncates the payload of a request or response in the log. Sets the limit of the LoggingFeature that the endpoint adds when loggingFeatureEnabled is true. Use -1 for no limit.
